population.note: FICTIONAL. There are about 275M adults. 27.5% current ≈ 75.6M; 39.5% ever-used ≈ 108.6M; used-and-off-now 12.0% ≈ 33.0M; never-used ≈ 166M. Ever-use rose 4.0 pts, inside the 5.5 limit. Cycling arithmetic: ≈14.0 pts of current users are on a second or later course and ≈5.0 pts of the off-now group restarted and then stopped again, so (14.0+5.0)/39.5 ≈ 48% cycled, up from 45%. That fits ~35% one-year persistence and ~40% restart, plus the January 2034 portal price rise and tighter gating, which pushed cash and commercial users off while public programmes re-enrolled others. Age check: 18–29 14.5% × 52M = 7.5M; 30–49 31% × 91M = 28.2M; 50–64 41.5% × 61M = 25.3M; 65+ 20.5% × 71M = 14.6M; total ≈ 75.6M. Income thirds average (30+28.5+24)/3 = 27.5. Growth came from four sources. (1) Medicare: the LIS copay was eliminated and more people aged into the benefit. 65+ use rose 3.5 pts, held back by bone pauses: about one in four 65+ ever-users is now off on a medically advised pause, a share pushed up by the Novo fracture disclosures. (2) The HRSA free-provision programme (CMAP), ≈1.2M users, mostly in the 10 states without enhanced match plus DC's neighbours. (3) Alcohol-use-disorder prescribing after the guideline endorsement, ≈1.4M users, mostly 30–64 men. (4) Off-label 'metabolic health' use among non-obese adults, ≈3.9M users, concentrated in the top third, which is why the top third rose most. Commercial users were the losses. Off-now (33M) now includes ≈2.4M who stopped because of the 2034 price rise or a gated-plan cut, and their regain is visible. Never-users are increasingly under-30s, rural residents of non-adopting states, people with contraindications, and a growing group who refuse after the scandal, centred on Tulsa, Atlanta and southwest Ohio. Pediatric: 0.9% of ~72M under-18s ≈ 650k, mostly adolescents 12+. FDA received the full adolescent bone dataset in mid-2034 and has not acted on it. About one child in three lives with a parent on, or cycling off, the drug.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Medicare Part D obesity benefit: $199 negotiated rate, contracted through 2035, and the 90-day bone-pause code, both unchanged. The FY2034 omnibus (Mar 2034) eliminated the $50 copay for Low-Income Subsidy enrollees: ≈2.2M LIS users × $50 × 12 ≈ $1.32B a year, shifted to the programme. Medicare pays ≈20.4% of fills ≈ 15.4M users (14.0M aged 65+ plus 1.4M disabled under 65): ≈6.4M diabetes and ≈9.0M obesity. Obesity gross: 9.0M × $199 × 12 ≈ $21.5B. Beneficiaries pay 6.8M non-LIS × $50 × 12 ≈ $4.1B, so the programme pays ≈$17.4B. All Medicare incretin fills: 15.4M × $199 × 12 ≈ $36.8B gross. Medicaid: 33 states plus DC on the 90% match and continuation standard (Pennsylvania and Wisconsin joined in 2033). ≈15.2% of fills ≈ 11.5M × $199 × 12 ≈ $27.5B gross before supplemental rebates. New: the HRSA Community Metabolic Access Program (CMAP) funds free provision through FQHCs, $3.6B a year appropriated: 1.2M users × $249 HRSA rate × 12 ≈ $3.59B. CMAP is aimed at uninsured adults and at non-adopting states, and it requires kiosk weigh-ins on the continuation-standard schedule. VA/DoD/IHS ≈1.1M users (1.5%), including VA alcohol-use-disorder prescribing. Excess hip fractures cost ≈16,000 × ~$45,000 ≈ $0.7B a year to Part A and Medicare Advantage. That cost is still unscored against the Part D benefit.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month, plus generic oral semaglutide and liraglutide–semaglutide combinations. China: generic semaglutide and early tirzepatide copies, and Chinese API remains the base of the gray trade. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 55–85. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt have generics. In the US the 2031 settlement allowed generic semaglutide entry in 2033, but FDA withheld final ANDA approval for both first filers in Feb 2033 after sterility findings at their Hyderabad and New Jersey fill-finish sites. Novo's authorised generic only triggers on a first-filer launch, so no US generic was on the market at the end of 2034. Tirzepatide exclusivity runs later.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Shock up. The expected 2033 generic cliff did not arrive, and a mid-2033 Section 232 increase on peptide API and finished injectables from India and China gave manufacturers a cost to cite. In Jan 2034 Lilly and Novo raised direct-portal injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide from $199–279 to $279–349, the first rise since 2025. Oral starting doses stayed at $149–150, while higher oral doses went from $199 to $249. Retatrutide is $479 direct ($1,499 list), amycretin $499 direct, and Lilly's tirzepatide–bimagrumab (Keystra) $749 direct ($1,899 list). PBM net under outcomes contracts rose to ≈$215–235. Commercial pharmacy trend ran ≈+11–12% in 2034. Gray-market delivered prices rose about a third under the tariff and parcel inspection, but the number of gray users still rose because the legal price rose more. Payer mix of ≈75.6M users: commercial 35.6% (26.9M), Medicare 20.4% (15.4M), Medicaid 15.2% (11.5M), CMAP 1.6% (1.2M), VA/DoD/IHS 1.5% (1.1M), cash/direct 20.2% (15.3M, including ≈2.6M 'calm'/'focus' subscribers and ≈3.9M non-obese 'metabolic health' users), imported/counterfeit 5.6% (4.2M); sum 75.6M. ≈80% of covering employers use outcome gating. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand. US incretin market ≈71.4M paying users × ≈$205 average net × 12 ≈ $176B.

GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, approved Mar 2033)
GLP-1 agonist / GIPR antagonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide, approved Oct 2033 with BMD warning)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist + activin type II receptor antibody combination (tirzepatide weekly + bimagrumab monthly: Keystra, approved Feb 2034)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder: guideline-endorsed second-line by ASAM and VA/DoD (Nov 2033), not yet FDA-labelled; semaglutide sNDA filed Jun 2034
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic health' and longevity regimens among non-obese adults (≈3.9M users): low-dose orals or monthly MariTide through concierge, longevity-clinic and telehealth channels, now mainstream in Austin, the Bay Area, Miami and Scottsdale
Keystra in non-obese 'body recomposition' and longevity protocols, sold as weight loss without the frailty
alcohol reduction below the AUD threshold, through EAP referral
'calm' and 'focus' subscriptions (≈2.6M, down from 3.5M after the 2033 label change and catalogue removals)
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS-endpoint trial still enrolling)
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The muscle_preserving_combo driver is met within the approval rules. Lilly filed the tirzepatide–bimagrumab BLA in Jan 2033 on phase 3 data showing ~22% mean weight loss with lean mass at ~10–12% of weight lost, against ~30–40% in untrained older users. FDA approved it 13 months later (Feb 2034) as Keystra. The label requires DEXA, carries muscle-spasm and acne warnings, and states that no fracture or falls benefit has been shown. The bone-density endpoint was neutral. Lilly's 'Keep what you built' campaign sells it as the end of skinny-frail, which the label does not support. Survodutide was approved Mar 2033 for chronic weight management. MariTide was approved Oct 2033 with a BMD Warning and DEXA requirement because of its GIPR-antagonist bone signal. The AUD driver is met by guideline endorsement (ASAM and VA/DoD, Nov 2033). The semaglutide AUD sNDA was filed Jun 2034, with a decision in 2035. The longevity driver is off-label and has no indication. Other bimagrumab combinations (with semaglutide) are in phase 3 and not filed. Best efficacy is still retatrutide 12 mg at 30%.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. Bimagrumab adds diarrhoea in the Keystra arm.
Rising in absolute numbers with high-dose retatrutide, survodutide and the larger 65+ population.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Counterfeit cases still confound reporting.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL litigation ongoing, with the first bellwether trial set for 2035.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A population problem. Medicare claims put ≈1.7M long-term older users at sarcopenia criteria, up from 1.3M. Keystra roughly halves the lean share of loss in trials, but only ≈0.5M people use it, mostly top-third and cash-pay, and grip-strength gains were smaller than the DEXA gains.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label retained; DEXA monitoring is in the retatrutide 12 mg, amycretin, MariTide and Keystra labels. Continuation standard 2.0 (Jul 2034) adds a kiosk grip or chair-stand check for long-term 65+ users. A CMS national coverage analysis of Keystra for sarcopenic older users opened in Sep 2034.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Third wave. ≈7.6M users aged 65+ with more than 2 years' use × ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × 0.35 excess ≈ 16,000 excess hip fractures a year against ~310,000 in the US, plus vertebral fractures among cycling postmenopausal women aged 50–64. Documents released in Novo's DOJ settlement showed an internal 2027 pooled fracture analysis in women 65+ that was submitted to FDA about 19 months late. DEXA waits eased to 10–16 weeks after CMS raised the DEXA fee in 2033.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA moved fracture risk into class-wide Warnings and Precautions in Oct 2033. Bone endpoints are required in filings. The Medicare bone-pause code continues, and gated private plans are still not bound by it. Novo is under a 5-year Corporate Integrity Agreement.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention; no class determination.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association, including in the AUD cohorts.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Acknowledged as uncommon across the class at standard doses, with an excess of roughly 1 in 100 to 1 in 200 users. Dose-dependent and higher at top triple-agonist doses (~12% vs ~5% on SHAPS at 12 mg retatrutide). The first independent survey of low-dose subscribers (2034) found rates near the class average, with wide intervals.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Jul 2033 class labelling lists 'decreased interest or pleasure (anhedonia)' as an uncommon adverse reaction, with dose-dependence noted for retatrutide. There is no boxed warning. FTC orders stand, and the major HR platforms dropped 'focus' listings.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Larger again. The 2034 price rise and gated-plan cuts added ≈2.4M involuntary stops on top of pauses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The bone-pause code softens it for Medicare. The Seventh Circuit has not ruled on the Indiana waiver.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency are common in high-loss older users, and some low-intake non-obese longevity users are now being seen.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; Part D counselling screen. No FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Twelve years of follow-up. The full adolescent bone-accrual dataset submitted in 2034 confirms lower BMD gain in a rapid-loss subset, and whether it reverses is unknown. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA adolescent review pending; postmarketing requirements continue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre calls are up modestly as gray users rose to ≈4.2M and buyers switched to cheaper, less-known vendors after the tariff.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts and seizures continue, and the 'Safe Pens' bill is still stalled. Individuals are not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in long-term 65+ users. Keystra users have shown no falls reduction yet.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening mandatory in the Part D counselling visit, and a strength check is now added.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded from emerging after three DEXA cohorts agreed. It is worst in over-50s cut off by price or gating.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint guidance recommends against elective stops in over-50s without a resistance-training plan; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mean resting heart-rate rise of several bpm at 12 mg retatrutide and with survodutide; arrhythmia significance unclear.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Precaution labelled; retatrutide CVOT readout expected 2035.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New. Muscle spasms (~1 in 4 early), diarrhoea and acne. Lean mass is preserved, but BMD is not improved and the benefit to muscle function lags the mass data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. The label states that no fracture or falls benefit has been shown.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New. A BMD decline beyond the weight-loss-expected amount in a subset, at the same time as the population fracture wave.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning and DEXA requirement in the label; postmarketing fracture study required.

food_and_beverage.state: With 27.5% of adults on the drug, salty-snack volume falls ~3% a year and confectionery ~4%. The decline slowed slightly as price-driven stoppers regained. Bone-forward dairy and protein lines still lead growth. A Keystra-adjacent 'build' protein category appeared in 2034. Private-equity candy owners do best in the discount channel and the gray-market-heavy regions.

alcohol.state: Seventh straight year of US spirits volume decline, at about −4%. The Nov 2033 AUD guideline moved prescribing into VA clinics and EAPs, and on-premise beer is down too. Distillers fund a 'moderation is a choice' campaign and quietly back the Ohio measure. Non-alcoholic and 'one good drink' premium formats hold.

restaurants.state: Spend per cover is roughly flat against 2032, the first pause in its decline, because some suburban diners came off after the January price rise. Gram-priced bowls stay standard. No-gram heritage rooms in Atlanta, Memphis and Houston and chain 'full table' nights are busier, helped by the backlash.

apparel.state: Size churn rose with price-driven stops. Resale and rental sized for cycling keep growing. Keystra marketing created a small 'kept-shoulders' athleisure line.

fitness.state: Still growing. DEXA-plus-coaching chains expand, and the CMS strength check fills senior strength classes. Medicare Advantage plans now argue over whether to fund prescribed lifting or a Keystra exception, and early CFO memos favour the cheaper lifting. Qualified trainers for older lifters remain the constraint.

insurance.state: Employer coverage fell from 66% to 61% after the January 2034 price rise, and ~80% of what remains is gated. Pharmacy trend runs ≈+11–12%. The 2033 tri-agency wellness rule lets employers tie up to a 30% premium differential to 'treated or explained' status, and large self-insured firms are adopting it. Life insurers keep asking untreated applicants with BMI ≥30 why. Medicare Advantage carries the fracture and rehabilitation costs.

pharma.state: Volume up ≈11% and price up. Lilly leads with tirzepatide, retatrutide 12 mg, Foundayo and Keystra. Novo paid $3.1B to settle with DOJ, its CEO left, it lost Medicare share to tirzepatide, and it is under a Corporate Integrity Agreement. Amgen's MariTide launched slowly behind its BMD warning. The Indian generic first filers took write-downs on the FDA findings, and India–US talks now include inspection reciprocity. DEXA and bone-agent makers keep winning.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on the drug is still unremarkable among insured over-40s. Being off has gained new legitimate reasons: 'price', 'they knew' (the Novo documents) and 'by conviction'. Visible regain now reads as either a price casualty or a protest. Among the affluent, a lean but square-shouldered build reads as Keystra, and lifted shoulders have stopped signalling discipline because a monthly injection can now produce them.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use is now 30/28.5/24 by income third, so the gap narrowed at the bottom through CMAP and Medicaid and widened at the top through non-obese longevity use. The quality gap is bigger. The top third has Keystra, scheduled DEXA and coaching. The bottom third has kiosk grip tests, FQHC pens with weigh-in schedules, or a $60 Hyderabad pen. Recomposition is the new class marker.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first meals remain standard. Full-table Sunday dinners have grown slightly as a backlash practice in Tulsa congregations and Atlanta collectives. 'Bring an off dish' is a potluck convention in southwest Ohio.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: The on/off/pausing field remains on apps. After the label change, 'Unmedicated' is more popular than at any time since 2030. Advice columns now field complaints about partners who started a 'metabolic' regimen without being overweight.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Still largely medicalised. The 2030 backlash coalition is now a visible political movement. The Novo documents turned it from an aesthetic objection into a grievance about consent. The Whole Body coalition joins Tulsa–Dallas 'appetite is a gift' churches, Atlanta body-sovereignty collectives, disability lawyers, natural-health influencers and, quietly, distillers. In November 2034 it won Ohio Issue 2 against weigh-in conditioning, 53–47.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Since the Jul 2033 class labelling, anhedonia is an 'uncommon' adverse reaction: an excess of roughly 0.5–1% at standard doses, and ~7 percentage points above comparator at 12 mg retatrutide. With ≈68M on standard doses that implies ≈350–700k excess cases. With ≈7M on top-dose triple or dual regimens it implies ≈450–500k. Both figures assume causality, and the two groups overlap in method rather than in people. Clinics now screen with two PHQ-style anhedonia questions at follow-up.
interior_life.framing: Side effect, uncommon and listed. Retail 'calm' language survives on the vendors' own sites, but the HR catalogues dropped 'focus' within a quarter of the label change and subscriptions fell from 3.5M to 2.6M. Users still say 'the grey', but they now say it to prescribers, who lower the dose or switch drugs. The cultural product moved to 'metabolic health', which promises longevity rather than mood.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Lifestyle-account reimbursement for 'focus' ended at most large employers after the label. Some longevity regimens are reimbursed instead through executive health benefits. Fleets and warehouses still favour continuous use. Union contracts now cite the anhedonia label in dose-adjustment grievances, and two contracts in 2034 copied the CMS bone-pause exemption and added a 'mood pause'.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Written unmedicated' got a second wind from the backlash, and Nashville labels market it again. Critics declared the 'grey era' over, though that may simply mean fewer people are on top doses. Alcohol-free club nights designed around AUD-prescribed regulars have opened in Columbus and Denver.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists now cite the label instead of anecdote. Dose holidays continue, and the 'restart' packs sell. Couples therapy deals with a new pattern: one partner prescribed for drinking whose personality the other partner no longer recognises, for better or worse.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Politics moved from who pays to consent and conditions. The Novo settlement lets the Whole Body coalition argue that weigh-ins police a drug whose risks were hidden. Republicans are split between accountability-conditioning and body-sovereignty voters. Democrats defend CMAP and the LIS copay cut while ducking the kiosk question. Ohio's vote makes conditioning a 2036 issue.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding and more aggressive after the scandal. It added class-wide fracture Warnings and anhedonia labelling, put a BMD warning on MariTide, approved Keystra with a label that disclaims fracture benefit, and withheld generic semaglutide approval on manufacturing grounds. Import enforcement is selective with no individual prosecutions. FTC continues claims policing. DOJ secured a $3.1B False Claims Act settlement with Novo.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The HRSA Community Metabolic Access Program provides free provision through FQHCs at $3.6B a year (≈1.2M users). The Part D LIS copay is eliminated (≈$1.32B a year). The permanent Part D obesity benefit stays at $199 with a $50 standard copay, and the 90% Medicaid match is taken by 33 states plus DC. VA prescribes for AUD under the 2033 guideline. There is no individual mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Continuation standard 2.0 (CMS rule Dec 2033, effective Jul 2034) keeps ≥80% PDC, six-monthly verified weights, the 5% response threshold, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users and the 90-day bone pause. It adds a kiosk grip or chair-stand test for long-term 65+ users, and CMAP inherits the same schedule. The 2033 tri-agency wellness rule allows employer premium differentials up to 30% tied to 'treated or explained' status. Ohio Issue 2 (Nov 2034) bans weigh-in conditions in Ohio state-funded benefits and public-employer plans from Jul 2035, which puts Ohio's enhanced match in conflict with CMS rules.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers toward tirzepatide. Fleets run DEXA for drivers over 55. The Army now allows accession waivers after 12 months' stability, matching the Air Force, while VA expands AUD prescribing to recent veterans.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The mid-2033 Section 232 increase on Indian and Chinese peptide API and finished injectables is the manufacturers' stated reason for the 2034 price rise. The FDA sterility findings at the two first filers' Hyderabad and New Jersey sites stalled US generic entry. India is pressing for inspection reciprocity under the 2032 trade framework. Chinese API still underlies the gray trade, which is now slower and costlier but larger.

events.event: FDA adds 'decreased interest or pleasure' to incretin labels as an uncommon side effect, dose-dependent for retatrutide; within weeks two major HR benefits platforms pull 'focus' subscriptions from their lifestyle catalogues

Novo Nordisk pays $3.1 billion to settle DOJ claims that it sat on a 2027 internal hip-fracture analysis in older women for 19 months; its chief executive resigns and FDA moves fracture risk into class-wide warnings the next month
ASAM and VA/DoD guidelines endorse semaglutide as a second-line treatment for alcohol use disorder; VA clinics begin prescribing it within the quarter, ahead of any FDA label

FDA approves Lilly's Keystra, a tirzepatide–bimagrumab combination filed in January 2033, with a label that says no fracture benefit has been shown; the 'Keep what you built' campaign launches at $749 a month direct and longevity clinics in Austin and Scottsdale start waitlists

Two months after Lilly and Novo raised portal pen prices to $279–349, the first rise since 2025, with generic semaglutide stalled since FDA withheld approval over sterility findings in February 2033, Congress funds $3.6 billion a year for free FQHC provision and drops the Part D copay for low-income seniors

Ohio voters pass Issue 2, 53–47, banning weigh-in conditions in state-funded benefits and public-employer plans, four months after CMS added a kiosk strength test to its continuation standard; CMS says Ohio's 90% match is 'under review'

open_tensions: Ohio Issue 2 takes effect in July 2035 and bans the weigh-ins that CMS requires for the 90% Medicaid match, so roughly 600k Ohio Medicaid users depend on a federal–state standoff, and copycat measures are being filed in Missouri and Michigan.

Keystra is sold as the end of skinny-frail, but its label says it has shown no fracture or falls benefit. Medicare's national coverage analysis must decide whether to pay several times the $199 rate for muscle mass that has not yet translated into fewer broken hips, while ≈16,000 excess hip fractures a year are billed to Part A and nobody scores them against Part D.

The generic semaglutide cliff that every 2031 budget assumed for 2033 has not arrived. Portal prices rose instead, employer coverage fell to 61%, and 4.2M people inject gray pens. Medicare's $199 contract runs out at the end of 2035 with no generic on the market to negotiate against.

Anhedonia is now on the label as uncommon and 'focus' was removed from HR catalogues, but ≈3.9M non-obese adults take the drug for 'metabolic health' and longevity. No outcome trial supports that use, and the label's mood warning was written for people who are taking it to treat obesity.
still_true: Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer direct channels.

The permanent Part D obesity benefit still pays the $199 negotiated rate, and the CMS 90-day 'bone pause' code still lets Medicare users stop without breaking continuation, while most gated employer plans still have no equivalent.
The 503B exclusion and the 503A injunction on compounded incretins still stand.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: They Knew About the Hips: Novo's $3.1B settlement, the $349 pen and the Ohio vote that said no to the scale
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 a little more than one American adult in four is on an incretin drug, and for the first time in years being off it does not need much explaining. Price is a reason, and so is the scandal. In parts of southwest Ohio, Tulsa and Atlanta, 'by conviction' has stopped being a confession and become a sign you put on the lawn.

The cliff did not come. The 2031 settlement allowed generic semaglutide in 2033, and every budget office planned around it. In February 2033 FDA inspectors found sterility failures at the fill-finish lines of both first filers. Novo's authorised generic only launches when a first filer does, so nothing launched. That summer a Section 232 increase landed on Indian and Chinese peptide ingredients. In January 2034 Lilly and Novo raised the federal portal price for weekly pens from $199–279 to $279–349, the first increase since 2025. The oral starter dose stayed at $149, so many people now step down to a pill instead of quitting. Employers responded the way employers do. Coverage fell from two-thirds of firms to about three in five, and nearly every plan still covering the drug is gated. A new wellness rule lets them charge up to thirty percent more in premiums to employees who are neither treated nor able to explain why.

Washington spent money and kept the conditions. In March Congress funded free provision through community health centres, $3.6 billion a year for about 1.2 million people, most in the states that never took the ninety-percent Medicaid match. It also ended the $50 copay for low-income seniors. Medicare still pays $199 under a contract that expires at the end of next year. Every public programme now uses the same kiosk by the blood-pressure cuff, and since July long-term users over sixty-five squeeze a grip sensor there as well as stepping on the scale.

That grip test is the bone story carried over to muscle. About sixteen thousand excess hip fractures a year are now attributed to long-term use among older Americans. In September 2033 the country learned that Novo had a version of that number in 2027 and gave it to regulators nineteen months late. The company paid $3.1 billion, its chief executive left, and fracture risk went into class-wide warnings. Lilly had already filed a combination of tirzepatide with bimagrumab, an antibody that spares muscle. It was approved in February as Keystra and marketed as the end of skinny-frail. On the scan it keeps most of the muscle. The label says plainly that it has not been shown to prevent a single fracture. It costs $749 a month, and the people buying it are mostly in Scottsdale and Austin, many of whom never had obesity. They take it for what their clinics call metabolic health. About four million such users are now on the drug, and no outcome trial supports what they are taking it for.

The quiet is now in the label. Since July 2033 decreased pleasure has been listed as an uncommon side effect. The HR platforms stopped listing 'focus' subscriptions within a quarter, and subscriptions have fallen by about a million. Doctors ask two questions about joy at every follow-up. The same drug is now guideline-recommended for alcohol use disorder, and VA clinics write the prescriptions. Spirits are in their seventh year of decline.

The counter-movement found its argument in the Novo documents. Their objection used to be that appetite is sacred. Now it is that you hid the risk and then made us weigh in. In November Ohio voted 53 to 47 to ban weigh-in conditions in state-funded benefits from next July. CMS says Ohio's enhanced match is under review, and nobody yet knows what happens to the six hundred thousand Ohioans who depend on it.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Carla Wendt is fifty-nine and runs the cafeteria at Belmont High in Dayton. On the first Tuesday in November she stands at the Kroger kiosk at 6:10 a.m. in her socks, because shoes add a pound and her school-district plan cuts people off at the second miss. The screen turns green.

Her mother is eighty-three and on Medicare, and she is on a bone pause. Carla's plan has no pause code. Her DEXA in August said osteopenia. Her rheumatologist wrote a letter, and the plan replied with a form.

At lunch the line wants the chili. She serves half portions to the kids whose parents filled in the form and full ones to the rest. Darnell from maintenance has been on it since spring for drinking, which the VA won't cover for him because he's not a veteran. He says Fridays feel like Wednesdays now. He says it like a weather report.

After work she takes her mother to the polling station at St. Albert's. A Whole Body volunteer hands out lawn signs. Her mother takes one and says, 'They knew about the hips,' the way she once said 'Watergate.'

Carla votes yes on Issue 2. She doesn't tell her sister, who drives to Cincinnati for Keystra and pays seven hundred and forty-nine dollars a month for it.

At home she opens the portal to check what her pen would cost if the plan drops her. It says $349. She closes it and puts the oral starter, $149, in the cart without buying it.

She eats the chili standing up and finishes it, and notices that she did.
